will be gr atefully accepted. dance in garvagh hall this friday, 23 october - music by the lakelanders - dancing 9 .00 – 12.00midnight. refreshments served. a heartfelt thank you dear friends, as i prepare to take up my new appointment as parish priest of drumragh (omagh) on 30th october, i wish to record my deep gratitude to you all for your kindness, support and genero sity, both in the life of the parishes and to me personally, for the last seven years. throughout my seven years of ministry in aghyaran and ardstraw west & castlederg, and three years in drumquin, i have been supported by wond erful teams of people who have walked with me and, on so many occasions, somehow made the impos sible possible! i feel very blessed to have been part of the faith story of the people of the three parishes and, i n thanking you for the very significant role you have played in inspiring an encouraging me in my own faith journey, i very much hope that, in some small way, my ministry among you has helped and encouraged you on your own journey of faith. i could never have managed without the help i have had in the parochial house, the office, our churches, our halls, graveyards and our schools. to our parish secretary, newsletter editor, sacristans, caretakers, school staff and volunteers: thank you. you kept everything going, often with little recogn ition or outward expressions of gratitude. and behind all of our liturgies there lies an ‘army’ of people – readers, eucharistic ministers, altar servers, musicians/choirs, collectors, counters, cleaners, groundsmen, caretakers – people who just show up faithfully and willingly, week in and week out. special thanks too to those who have given of their gifts, knowledge and time on parish committees including the various fundraising groups, parish tea group, children’s liturgy and, more recently, on our leadership teams. i am indebted also to the staff and children of our schools for their warm welcome at all times and their co-operation and willingness to share in the life of our churches and parishes. i have been privileged to accompany many families and individuals on milestone occasions in their lives over the last seven years. it is always wonderful to share with families in the happy, joyful occasions – the baptisms, weddings, golden weddings, first communions, confirmations and other a chievements. part of priestly ministry of course is journeying with families in their darkest hours – families facing illness, death and the loss of loved ones, sometimes in the most heartbreaking circumstances. it has been a privilege for me to have walked with many families in sad, difficulty and challenging times in their lives. again, i have found the faith and courage shown by so many families at such times to be deeply humbling, and a s ource of strength and reassurance to me in my own faith. an important part of any priest's ministry is visiting and bringing the eucharist to those who are housebound or unable to come to church. visitation of the housebound in our parishes has been a very privileged part of my ministry; so too has visitation of our nursing homes. we came through covid together, and we've shared seven christmases and easters. i won't forge t any of this! in recent years it has also been a joy to have fr thomas minister alongside me. his generosity and helpfulness have been a great blessing. thank you, fr thomas, for all your support. thanks too to fr gilmore for his wise counsel, and to fr peter mccawille for the generous help he continues to give to us all. i leave with a heavy heart, but also with memories of friendship and neighbourliness that, for me, make the gospel come alive. last but not least, i want to say a word of welcome to my successo r, fr chris. there are a good many projects underway or just about to begin, but fr chris is talented, capable and hardwor king, and i have no worries on that score. with your help and encouragement, and with his leadership, i know the p eople of these three parishes will grow stronger in faith and keep the light of the gospel burning brightly, a beacon of hope in a fragile world. i hope fr chris will be as happy here as i have been, and i ask god's blessing on all that you do together. please keep me in your thoughts and prayers. i'll always keep the people of this pastoral area in mine, asking that god will reward you for all your goodness and kindness. with love and gratitude, fr paul

october at 7.30pm. a warm welcome to fr paul fraser we are delighted to extend a very warm welcome to fr paul fraser, who has been appointed parish priest of drumragh. a native of derry city, fr paul was ordained to the priesthood in st patrick’s church, pennyburn, on 1 june 1986. following three years of ministry in buncrana, co donegal, he undertook teacher training at st mary’s, strawberry hill, london. he subsequently served as a teacher and chaplain at st columb’s college in derry. over his forty years of priestly ministry, fr paul has gained a wealth of pastoral and educational experience, including appointments in the archdiocese of los angeles and the diocese of arundel and brighton, where, alongside his parish responsibilities, he also taught psychology and ict. in 2015, he returned to derry as curate in st mary’s parish, creggan, before moving to tyrone in 2019 as parish priest of ardstraw west, castlederg and aghyaran. three years ago, drumquin (langfield) was added to these parishes, forming the west tyrone pastoral area. fr paul now comes to drumragh at an important time in the life of our diocese, as we respond to changing circumstances and seek new ways of working together to build strong and vibrant parish communities. he is looking forward to the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead for the church in the omagh area. we wish fr paul every blessing as he begins his ministry among us. let us keep him in our prayers and give him our wholehearted support, not only through our words of welcome, but through our presence, our encouragement and our active participation in the life and mission of the parish.
